main_text.head: De tribus diuersis lactis partibus, ferosa, caseosa, & butyrosa.
main_text.p: TRes in lacte substantias contineri, & praeter has nullam esse quartam, quae lactis nomine designetur, sed totum, quod ex iis tribus legitime temperatis constit, lactis nomen sibi assumere, in confesso est.

Serum quid? & unde dicatur?Serum vnumquodq; lactis genus continet, estq; aquosior & tenuior lactis substantia, à qua caseus, hoc est, crassior & densior pars est separata: graecis ὀρὸς dicitur, quasi separatum à ὁρίζω, id est, findo, sepáro, germ. Molcken. Porro antiquitati celebratissimum semper fuit, obq; vim abstergendi, attenuandi, aluumq; abluendæ ac soluendæ nobilitatum, hodie caprinum in laude magis habet. Estq; serum ipsum tanto melius ac praestantius, quanto lac ipsum melius fuerit. Porro de temperatura seri autores, & inter se & à Galeno dissentire videntur: alii enim calidum, alii frigidum esse contendunt. Galenus lib.4.simpl.medicam. frigidum, libro vero 10. sicut & libro 3.alimentor. calidum id esse affe-rit. Qui serum simpliciter & absolutè idio-tarum

page.notes: Running head reads "De Vita" at top; the line beneath it is the continuation from the previous page, printed as "iffe Plutarehus lib.4.Sympofiacorum scriptum reliquit." The first word is doubtful (read as "isse [?]"), and "Plutarehus" is a printing error for Plutarchus, left as printed. The Greek words ὀρὸς and ὁρίζω are doubtful and the second may be ἀφορίζω; both are marked for checking. "Molcken" is set in black letter within roman text. The left margin note is in italics. The bottom word "tarum" is the catchword, followed by "idio-" at the line end.
